examples.ko: 그 태풍은 마을에 파괴적인 피해를 줬어요.
examples.en: That typhoon did devastating damage to the town.
Stress has a destructive effect on your health.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 한 말은 너무 파괴적이에요.
examples.en: What that person said is so destructive.

examples.ko: 파괴적인 습관은 빨리 고치는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to fix destructive habits quickly.

examples.ko: 화가 나면 파괴적으로 행동하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people act destructively when they get angry.

examples.ko: 새로운 기술이 시장에 파괴적인 변화를 가져왔어요.
examples.en: The new technology brought disruptive change to the market.

explain: '파괴적인', '파괴적이다'처럼 쓰고, 뒤에 '-인'을 붙여 명사를 꾸미는 경우가 가장 많아요. 태풍 같은 큰 피해뿐 아니라 '파괴적인 습관', '파괴적인 변화'처럼 나쁜 영향이나 기존 질서를 크게 바꾸는 것에도 써요. 반대말은 '건설적'이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '파괴적인' before a noun, or as '파괴적이다'. It covers big damage like a typhoon, but also '파괴적인 습관' (destructive habit) and '파괴적인 변화' (disruptive change). The opposite is '건설적' (constructive).

examples.ko: 어머니가 만든 파김치는 밥이랑 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: My mother's green onion kimchi is delicious with rice.
Green onion kimchi smells strong, but I like it.
Try eating ramen with green onion kimchi on top.
I bought a container of green onion kimchi at the market.
The green onion kimchi is well fermented, so even the juice is tasty.
I walked all day and now I'm completely wiped out.

explain: 파로 담근 김치예요. 소금에 절인 파가 축 늘어진 모습에서, '파김치가 되다'는 몹시 지쳐 기운이 없다는 비유로 써요. '녹초가 되다'와 비슷하지만 더 편한 입말이에요.

phrases.example: 야근하고 집에 오니 완전히 파김치가 됐어요.
phrases.en: After working overtime, I got home totally wiped out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몹시 지쳐서 축 늘어졌을 때 쓰는 편한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say you are so tired you have gone limp.

explain_en: It is kimchi made with green onions. Salted green onions go limp, so '파김치가 되다' is used figuratively for being completely drained of energy. It is close to '녹초가 되다' but more colloquial.

examples.ko: 여름에는 해수욕장마다 파라솔과 튜브를 빌려주는 가게가 생겨요.
examples.en: In summer, shops that rent out parasols and tubes appear at every beach.

examples.ko: 햇빛이 너무 강하니까 파라솔 아래에 앉아요.
examples.en: The sun is too strong, so let's sit under the parasol.

examples.ko: 카페 밖에 파라솔이 있어서 앉기 편해요.
examples.en: There are parasols outside the cafe, so it's comfortable to sit.
The wind blew and the parasol almost flew away.
I put up the parasol and read a book in the shade.

examples.ko: 파라솔 하나에 의자가 네 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are four chairs for each parasol.

explain: 손에 드는 양산이 아니라 바닷가나 카페 야외 자리에 세워 두는 큰 우산을 말할 때 주로 써요. 손에 드는 것은 '양산'이라고 해요. 보통 '파라솔을 펴다/접다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It usually means a large umbrella set up at a beach or an outdoor cafe, not one you carry. The handheld sun umbrella is called '양산'. You say '파라솔을 펴다/접다' (open/close).

examples.en: I bought a fly swatter to catch flies.
Do you know where the fly swatter is?

examples.ko: 여름이 되면 집집마다 파리채가 하나씩 있어요.
examples.en: When summer comes, every house has a fly swatter.
I tried to swat a mosquito with the fly swatter and broke a cup.
Grandma went to the kitchen holding a fly swatter.

examples.ko: 이 파리채는 손잡이가 길어서 쓰기 편해요.
examples.en: This fly swatter has a long handle, so it's easy to use.

explain: '파리'에 도구를 뜻하는 '채'가 붙은 말이에요. 파리뿐 아니라 모기나 벌레를 잡을 때도 써요. 보통 '파리채로 때리다/잡다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It combines '파리' (fly) with '채', a word for a handheld tool. People also use it for mosquitoes and other bugs. You say '파리채로 때리다/잡다'.

examples.ko: 그 커플은 결혼식 한 달 전에 파혼했어요.
examples.en: That couple broke off their engagement a month before the wedding.
Our values were too different, so we decided to call off the engagement.
I heard the news that my friend suddenly broke off her engagement.

examples.ko: 드라마에서 두 사람은 오해 때문에 파혼해요.
examples.en: In the drama, the two break off their engagement because of a misunderstanding.
If you break off the engagement, what happens to the wedding hall fee?
We almost broke off the engagement because of my parents' objection.

explain: 약혼이나 결혼 약속을 깼을 때 써요. 이미 결혼한 사이가 헤어지는 것은 '이혼하다'라고 해요. 한 사람이 일방적으로 깰 때는 '파혼을 통보하다'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when an engagement or a promise to marry is broken. For couples already married, the word is '이혼하다' (divorce). When one side does it alone, people say '파혼을 통보하다' (announce the break-off).

examples.en: There is a fruit stand at the entrance of the mart.

examples.ko: 신제품이 판매대 맨 앞에 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: The new product is placed at the very front of the display stand.
A staff member handed out samples at the sales stand.
I bought socks at a stand in front of the subway station.
They rearranged the stand, so it looks nicer.

examples.ko: 이 책은 서점 판매대에 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: This book is stacked on the sales table in the bookstore.

explain: 가게 안이나 길가에서 물건을 쌓아 두고 파는 대(臺)를 말해요. 큰 가게의 '매장'보다 작고, 물건을 올려놓은 자리 자체를 가리켜요. '가판대'는 길에 놓인 것을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the stand or table where goods are piled up and sold, inside a shop or on the street. It is smaller than a '매장' (store) and points to the spot itself. For one on the street, '가판대' is often used.

examples.ko: 올해 판매액이 작년보다 두 배 늘었어요.
examples.en: This year's sales amount doubled compared to last year.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 하루 판매액이 꽤 높아요.
examples.en: This shop's daily sales are quite high.

examples.ko: 행사 기간 동안 판매액의 일부를 기부해요.
examples.en: During the event, part of the sales will be donated.
I organized the monthly sales in a table.
Sales went up, but profit went down.

examples.ko: 온라인 판매액이 처음으로 매장 판매액을 넘었어요.
examples.en: For the first time, online sales exceeded in-store sales.

explain: 물건을 판 돈의 총액이에요. 뉴스나 회사 보고서에 자주 나와요. '매출'과 거의 같게 쓰지만 일상 대화에서는 '매출'이 더 흔해요. '판매량'은 팔린 개수라서 달라요.
explain_en: It is the total amount of money from goods sold, common in news and company reports. It is used almost like '매출', but '매출' is more common in daily talk. '판매량' is the number of items sold, which is different.

examples.en: They handed out tumblers as promotional items at the event.
Our company makes promotional items every year.
This pen is a freebie I got from the bank.

examples.ko: 판촉물이 예뻐서 일부러 그 가게에 갔어요.
examples.en: The freebie was so cute that I went to that shop on purpose.

examples.ko: 판촉물은 로고가 들어가 있는 게 많아요.
examples.en: Many promotional items have a logo on them.
If you buy the new product, we give you a promotional item.

explain: 물건을 더 팔려고 손님에게 나눠 주는 선물이나 홍보용 물건이에요. 가게에서 그냥 주는 작은 선물은 '사은품'이라고도 해요. 회사 일에서 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: These are gifts or promotional goods handed to customers to help sell more. A small gift from a shop is also called '사은품'. It is a word often used in business.

examples.en: A stop sign is shaped like an octagon.
We drew an octagon in math class.
An octagon has eight sides.
This pavilion is unusual because its roof is an octagon.
Shall we make octagon-shaped cookies?
A regular octagon has sides that are all the same length.

explain: '삼각형, 사각형, 오각형…'처럼 각의 수에 '형'을 붙인 도형 이름이에요. 도로의 정지 표지판 모양으로 가장 쉽게 떠올릴 수 있어요. 변과 각이 모두 같은 것은 '정팔각형'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It follows the pattern of '삼각형, 사각형, 오각형' — a shape named by its number of angles. The easiest example is a road stop sign. One with all sides and angles equal is a '정팔각형' (regular octagon).

examples.en: This chair has armrests, so it's comfortable.

examples.ko: 비행기 팔걸이는 옆 사람과 같이 쓰는 거예요.
examples.en: The airplane armrest is shared with the person next to you.
I watched the movie with my arm on the armrest.

examples.ko: 소파 팔걸이가 낡아서 천을 새로 씌웠어요.
examples.en: The sofa armrest was worn out, so I put new fabric on it.

examples.ko: 팔걸이를 올리면 침대처럼 누울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you lift the armrest, you can lie down like on a bed.

examples.ko: 팔걸이 없는 의자가 더 가볍고 싸요.
examples.en: Chairs without armrests are lighter and cheaper.

explain: 의자, 소파, 자동차 좌석 옆에서 팔을 올려놓는 부분이에요. 비행기나 영화관 좌석에서는 옆 사람과 같이 쓰기도 해요. 보통 '팔걸이가 있다/없다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the part beside a chair, sofa or car seat where you rest your arm. On planes or in cinemas you may share it with the person next to you. You often say '팔걸이가 있다/없다'.

en: pillowing one's head on someone's arm; pillow of one's arm

examples.ko: 그는 팔베개를 하고 누워서 천장을 봤어요.
examples.en: He lay with his arm under his head and looked at the ceiling.
The child fell asleep with Dad's arm as a pillow.
If you give someone an arm pillow, your arm goes numb.
I lay on the grass with my arm as a pillow and watched the clouds.

examples.ko: 남편이 팔베개를 해 줘서 금방 잠이 왔어요.
examples.en: My husband gave me his arm as a pillow, so I fell asleep quickly.
We talked for a long time lying with an arm pillow.

explain: '팔베개를 하다'는 자기 팔을 베는 것도, 남에게 자기 팔을 베게 해 주는 것도 돼요. 이때는 '해 주다'를 붙여서 구분해요. 편하게 눕거나 가까운 사이에서 하는 모습을 말해요.
explain_en: '팔베개를 하다' can mean using your own arm as a pillow, or letting someone else rest on your arm; add '해 주다' for the latter. It describes a relaxed lying posture, or something done between close people.

examples.en: We ordered palbochae at the Chinese restaurant and shared it.
Palbochae has lots of seafood and vegetables in it.

examples.ko: 저는 매운 것보다 팔보채가 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I like palbochae more than spicy food.

examples.ko: 이 집 팔보채는 새우가 정말 커요.
examples.en: The shrimp in this place's palbochae are really big.
One palbochae and one fried rice, please.
Palbochae was the most popular dish at the family gathering.

explain: 해산물, 고기, 채소를 넣고 걸쭉한 소스로 볶은 중국식 요리예요. 한국 중식당에서는 여럿이 나눠 먹는 큰 접시 요리로 주문해요. 한 그릇으로 먹는 짜장면, 짬뽕과 달라요.
explain_en: It is a Chinese-style dish of seafood, meat and vegetables stir-fried in a thick sauce. In Korean Chinese restaurants it is ordered as a large plate to share. Unlike jajangmyeon or jjamppong, it is not a single-bowl meal.

examples.ko: 요즘은 회갑보다 칠순이나 팔순에 잔치를 하는 집이 많아요.
examples.en: These days, more families hold a party for the 70th or 80th birthday than the 60th.
We held Grandfather's 80th birthday party at a restaurant.

examples.ko: 다음 달이 어머니 팔순이라서 선물을 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: Next month is my mother's 80th birthday, so I'm thinking about a gift.
We gave flowers to our teacher, who turned eighty.
Even though she is over eighty, she is really vigorous.

examples.ko: 가족이 모여 팔순 기념 여행을 다녀왔어요.
examples.en: The family got together and took a trip for the 80th birthday.

explain: 여든 살 또는 여든 번째 해를 가리키는 말이라서 보통 어르신의 생신을 말할 때 써요. '환갑(회갑), 칠순, 팔순, 구순'처럼 나이마다 잔치 이름이 있어요. 높임말로 '팔순을 맞으시다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to age eighty and is used for an elder's birthday. Koreans have names for milestone celebrations: '환갑(회갑), 칠순, 팔순, 구순'. For honorific speech, say '팔순을 맞으시다'.

examples.ko: 그는 회사를 몰래 다른 회사에 팔아넘겼어요.
examples.en: He secretly sold the company off to another company.

examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 쓰던 가구를 다 팔아넘겼어요.
examples.en: Before moving, I sold off all the furniture I'd been using.

examples.ko: 친구를 팔아넘기는 사람은 믿을 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't trust someone who sells out his friends.
I'm trying to dump the leftover stock cheaply.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 내 정보를 업체에 팔아넘겼대요.
examples.en: I heard that person sold my information to a company.

examples.ko: 헌 물건을 한꺼번에 팔아넘겼더니 속이 시원해요.
examples.en: I sold off all the old stuff at once, and I feel relieved.

explain: 그냥 '팔다'와 달리 값이나 상대를 가리지 않고 한꺼번에 처분한다는 느낌이 있어요. 사람, 정보, 회사처럼 팔면 안 되는 것에 쓰면 배신이나 나쁜 행동이라는 뉘앙스가 강해요. 목적어에 따라 느낌이 많이 달라져요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '팔다', it feels like getting rid of something in one go without caring about price or buyer. With people, information or companies, it carries a strong sense of betrayal. The tone changes a lot depending on the object.

examples.en: Grandfather is over eighty, but he's still full of energy.
After a good sleep, my body feels full of energy.
I bought a lively fresh fish at the market.
Kids get full of energy when it's time to play.
I'm still full of life, so don't worry.

examples.ko: 감기가 다 나아서 요즘은 팔팔하게 지내요.
examples.en: My cold is all gone, so I've been doing great lately.

explain: '건강하다'보다 기운이 넘치고 생생하다는 느낌이 강하고, 나이 든 분이나 살아 있는 생선에도 자주 써요. 보통 몸이 튼튼하고 활기 있을 때 말해요. 높임은 '팔팔하세요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It feels more full of vigor than '건강하다' and is often said of elders or live fresh fish. It describes a body that is strong and lively. The honorific form is '팔팔하세요'.

en: fashion industry; the world of fashion

examples.en: That designer is very famous in the fashion world.
Trends change fast in the fashion world.
My dream is to work in the fashion industry.
This season's talk of the fashion world is jeans.

examples.ko: 패션계 사람들은 옷을 정말 잘 입어요.
examples.en: People in the fashion industry dress really well.
Even the overseas fashion world is paying attention to Korean designers.

explain: '-계'는 '연예계, 정치계, 의료계'처럼 어떤 분야의 사람들과 세계를 가리켜요. '패션 업계'는 회사와 산업 쪽, '패션계'는 디자이너·모델까지 포함한 분야 전체 느낌이에요. 보통 '패션계에서 일하다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: The suffix '-계' means a field and the people in it, as in '연예계, 정치계, 의료계'. '패션 업계' leans toward companies and industry, while '패션계' feels like the whole field including designers and models. You often say '패션계에서 일하다'.

examples.en: I boiled soybean paste stew with enoki mushrooms.
Cut off the base of the enoki mushrooms and wash them.

examples.ko: 고기를 팽이버섯에 말아서 구워 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: It's tasty to roll meat around enoki mushrooms and grill it.
I bought a pack of enoki mushrooms at the mart.
Shabu-shabu isn't the same without enoki mushrooms.
Enoki mushrooms get chewy if you cook them too long.

explain: 가늘고 길며 하얀색이 많은 버섯이에요. 찌개, 전골, 샤브샤브에 많이 넣고, 너무 오래 끓이면 질겨지니까 마지막에 넣는 경우가 많아요. 표고버섯, 느타리버섯과 모양이 달라요.
explain_en: It is a thin, long, mostly white mushroom. It goes into stews, hot pots and shabu-shabu, and is often added at the end because it gets chewy when overcooked. Its shape differs from shiitake or oyster mushrooms.

examples.en: The bird is caught in the net and keeps flapping its wings.
The fish at the market are still flopping around.
The pigeon flapped and flew up into the sky.
The caught fish flopped on the floor.
I woke up to the sound of a chicken flapping.

examples.ko: 새가 퍼덕거리다가 힘이 빠졌는지 가만히 있어요.
examples.en: The bird flapped around and now seems to have run out of strength, sitting still.

explain: 새가 날개를 치거나 물고기가 몸을 세게 흔드는 모습을 계속해서 보여 줄 때 써요. 한 번만 하는 느낌의 '퍼덕이다'와 달리 '-거리다'가 붙어서 반복되는 움직임이에요. 소리와 움직임이 같이 느껴지는 말이에요.
explain_en: It shows a bird beating its wings or a fish thrashing its body again and again. The '-거리다' ending gives a repeated movement, unlike the single-motion feel of '퍼덕이다'. It suggests both sound and motion.

en: shovel food into one's mouth; scoop and eat

examples.en: I scooped up and ate a whole tub of ice cream, and now my stomach hurts.

examples.ko: 밥을 숟가락으로 퍼먹지 말고 천천히 먹어요.
examples.en: Don't shovel your rice in with a spoon; eat slowly.

examples.ko: 스트레스를 받으면 단 걸 퍼먹게 돼요.
examples.en: When I'm stressed, I end up stuffing myself with sweets.

examples.ko: 동생이 냉장고 앞에서 케이크를 퍼먹고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger brother is shoveling cake into his mouth in front of the fridge.
I was hungry, so I scooped up the stew with a spoon and wolfed it down.
It tastes good while stuffing myself, but I regret it later.

explain: 음식을 숟가락으로 푹푹 퍼서 많이, 급하게 먹는 모습이에요. 예의 바른 표현은 아니라서 친구나 가족끼리 편하게 말할 때 써요. 어른께는 '많이 드세요'처럼 말해야 해요.
explain_en: It shows scooping food in big spoonfuls and eating a lot, fast. It is not polite, so use it casually with friends or family. To elders, say something like '많이 드세요' instead.

examples.ko: 생일 선물로 하트 모양 펜던트를 받았어요.
examples.en: I got a heart-shaped pendant as a birthday gift.
The pendant on my necklace came off, so I took it for repair.
This pendant was handed down by my grandmother.
If you just change the pendant, the whole look changes.

examples.ko: 작은 펜던트가 달린 목걸이를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a necklace with a small pendant.

examples.ko: 펜던트 안에 사진을 넣을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can put a photo inside the pendant.

explain: 목걸이 줄 끝에 달려 있는 장식을 말해요. 줄까지 포함한 전체는 '목걸이'라고 하고, 장식 부분만 가리킬 때 '펜던트'라고 해요. '펜던트 조명'처럼 천장에 매다는 등을 가리키기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the ornament hanging on a necklace chain. The whole piece with the chain is a '목걸이', and '펜던트' points to the charm part. It can also mean a hanging ceiling light, as in '펜던트 조명'.

examples.en: I looked for pliers to cut the wire.
I pulled out the nail with pliers.
There should be a pair of pliers in the toolbox.
My father fixed the bike chain with pliers.

examples.ko: 펜치 좀 빌려 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you lend me your pliers?

examples.ko: 이 펜치는 손잡이가 미끄럽지 않아서 좋아요.
examples.en: These pliers are good because the handles aren't slippery.

explain: 물건을 잡거나 철사를 자르고 구부릴 때 쓰는 공구예요. 손잡이를 쥐어 물건을 꽉 집어요. 끝이 뾰족한 것은 '롱노즈'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a tool for gripping, cutting and bending wire. You squeeze the handles to hold things tightly. The pointed-tip type is often called '롱노즈'.

examples.en: I caught a cold and my tonsils are swollen.
Because of my tonsils, it's hard to swallow saliva.
The doctor checked my tonsils.
I had tonsil surgery when I was a child.
My tonsils tend to swell often, so I'm careful.
I ate cold food and now my tonsils hurt.

explain: 목 안쪽 양옆에 있는 부분이에요. 목이 아플 때 '편도선이 부었다'고 자주 말해요. 염증이 생긴 병은 '편도선염'이라고 해요.
explain_en: These are the glands on both sides at the back of the throat. When your throat hurts, people often say '편도선이 부었다'. The inflamed condition is called '편도선염' (tonsillitis).

examples.ko: 그분은 교장이 되지 않고 평교사로 정년을 맞았어요.
examples.en: He retired as a regular teacher without becoming a principal.

examples.ko: 저는 승진보다 평교사로 아이들을 가르치고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd rather teach kids as a regular teacher than get promoted.

examples.ko: 평교사도 학교 일에 의견을 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Regular teachers can also give opinions on school matters.

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 평교사가 학년 회의를 이끌어요.
examples.en: At our school, regular teachers lead the grade meetings.

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 부장 교사에서 다시 평교사가 되셨어요.
examples.en: That teacher went back to being a regular teacher after being a department head.
A regular teacher's salary varies by experience.

explain: 교장, 교감, 부장 같은 직책이 없는 일반 교사를 가리켜요. '평-'은 '평사원'처럼 직책이 없는 사람 앞에 붙기도 해요. 뉴스나 학교 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means an ordinary teacher with no title such as principal, vice principal or department head. The prefix '평-' also appears in words like '평사원' for people without a rank. It often shows up in news and school talk.

examples.ko: 체조 선수가 평균대 위에서 균형을 잡았어요.
examples.en: The gymnast kept her balance on the balance beam.
A balance beam is only 10 centimeters wide.
My daughter fell while practicing on the balance beam.
The backward turn on the balance beam is hard.
She advanced to the balance beam final at this competition.

examples.ko: 평균대 위에서는 시선을 앞에 두는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: On the balance beam, it's important to keep your eyes ahead.

explain: 여자 체조 종목에 쓰는 좁고 긴 기구와 그 종목 이름이에요. 이름에 '평균'이 들어가지만 숫자의 평균이 아니라 균형(평균)을 잡는다는 뜻의 한자어예요. 그래서 수학 시간의 '평균'과는 관계가 없어요.
explain_en: It is the narrow, long apparatus used in women's gymnastics, and also the event's name. '평균' here refers to balance, not the mathematical average, so it has nothing to do with the '평균' in math class.

examples.ko: 올해 매출은 어땠어요? — 기복은 있었지만 평균적으로는 지난해와 비슷해요.
examples.en: How were sales this year? — There were ups and downs, but on average they're similar to last year.

examples.ko: 한국 사람은 평균적으로 하루에 몇 시간 자요?
examples.en: On average, how many hours a day do Koreans sleep?

examples.ko: 평균적인 가정의 한 달 생활비를 조사했어요.
examples.en: We surveyed the monthly living costs of an average household.

examples.ko: 이 반 학생들은 평균적으로 키가 큰 편이에요.
examples.en: The students in this class are tall on average.
My grades are a bit above the average level.

examples.ko: 평균적으로 보면 여름에 전기를 가장 많이 써요.
examples.en: On average, people use the most electricity in summer.

explain: '평균적으로'는 '보통 이 정도로'라는 뜻으로 문장 앞에서 자주 써요. '평균적인 + 명사'로 꾸밀 때도 많아요. 예외는 있지만 전체로 보면 그렇다는 느낌을 줘요.
explain_en: '평균적으로' is often placed early in a sentence to say 'typically, about this much'. It also appears as '평균적인 + noun'. It signals that there are exceptions, but overall that's how it is.

examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 집 평면도를 먼저 봤어요.
examples.en: I looked at the floor plan of the house before moving.
The real estate agent sent me the floor plan.
Looking at the floor plan, the rooms are smaller than I thought.

examples.ko: 가구를 놓기 전에 평면도에 치수를 적어 봤어요.
examples.en: Before placing furniture, I wrote the measurements on the floor plan.

examples.ko: 이 건물 평면도는 입구에 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: The floor plan of this building is posted at the entrance.

examples.ko: 평면도만으로는 천장 높이를 알 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't tell the ceiling height from the floor plan alone.

explain: 집이나 건물을 위에서 내려다본 모양으로 그린 그림이에요. 집을 구할 때 방, 화장실, 베란다 위치를 확인하는 데 쓰고, '집 구조'를 이야기할 때 같이 나와요. 옆에서 본 그림은 '입면도'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a drawing of a home or building as seen from above. When house hunting, it is used to check the position of rooms, bathroom and balcony. A side-view drawing is called '입면도'.

en: ordinary clothes; everyday clothes; casual clothes

examples.en: As soon as I got home, I changed out of my going-out clothes into everyday clothes.
You can come to today's gathering in casual clothes.
I went to the bank in everyday clothes.
I wear a suit to work and everyday clothes on weekends.
Even everyday clothes make a good impression if worn neatly.
It's not a party, so please come in everyday clothes.

explain: 특별한 자리가 아닌 평소에 입는 편한 옷이에요. 반대말은 '정장'이나 '예복'이고, 일상 대화에서는 '편한 옷', '사복'이라고도 해요. 학교나 군대에서 제복이 아닌 옷은 '사복'이라고 해요.
explain_en: These are comfortable clothes worn on ordinary occasions. The opposites are '정장' or '예복', and in daily talk people also say '편한 옷' or '사복'. Clothes that aren't a school or military uniform are called '사복'.

en: for one's lifetime; in one's whole life

examples.ko: 선생님의 말씀을 평생토록 잊지 못할 거예요.
examples.en: I will never forget my teacher's words for the rest of my life.
Grandmother lived her whole life farming.
I'll repay this kindness for the rest of my life.

examples.ko: 그는 평생토록 한 가지 일만 했어요.
examples.en: He did just one kind of work his whole life.
Let's stay good friends for our whole lives.
Don't do something you'll regret your whole life.

explain: '평생'에 '끝까지'의 느낌을 더해서 태어나서 죽을 때까지 계속된다는 뜻을 강조해요. 글이나 감동적인 말에 어울려서 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '평생'이라고 하는 경우가 더 많아요. 뒤에는 '잊지 못하다', '살다'처럼 오래 이어지는 말이 와요.
explain_en: It adds a feeling of 'all the way to the end' to '평생', stressing that something lasts from birth until death. It suits writing and heartfelt speech, while everyday talk often uses plain '평생'. It pairs with long-lasting expressions like '잊지 못하다' or '살다'.

examples.en: I'm more comfortable with the breaststroke than freestyle.
I learned the breaststroke kick in swimming class.
In the breaststroke, you move your arms and legs together.
I timed my 100-meter breaststroke.
That athlete won the gold medal in the breaststroke.

examples.ko: 평영을 할 때는 머리를 물 밖으로 내밀어요.
examples.en: When doing the breaststroke, you lift your head out of the water.

explain: 수영 영법의 하나로, 개구리처럼 팔다리를 모았다 펴며 나아가요. 다른 영법은 '자유형, 배영, 접영'이라고 해요. 개구리 영법이라는 느낌이라 '개구리헤엄'이라고 부르는 사람도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a swimming style where you pull your arms and legs in and push out like a frog. The other strokes are '자유형, 배영, 접영'. Some people call it '개구리헤엄' (frog swim).

examples.ko: 다 쓴 건전지는 폐건전지 수거함에 넣어요.
examples.en: Put used batteries in the waste battery collection box.
There is a waste battery collection box in front of the community center.

examples.ko: 폐건전지는 일반 쓰레기와 따로 버려야 해요.
examples.en: Waste batteries must be thrown away separately from regular trash.
I took the waste batteries I had collected.
Waste batteries contain substances that harm the environment.
We did an activity of collecting waste batteries with the kids.

explain: 더 이상 쓸 수 없게 된 건전지를 말해요. 한국에서는 일반 쓰레기로 버리지 않고 주민센터나 아파트 단지에 있는 전용 수거함에 모으는 경우가 많아요. 재활용 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: These are batteries that can no longer be used. In Korea they are usually not thrown away with regular trash but put into special boxes at community centers or apartment complexes. The word often appears in talk about recycling.

examples.ko: 자주 가던 서점이 다음 달에 폐점해요.
examples.en: The bookstore I often visited is closing down next month.

examples.ko: 손님이 줄어서 결국 가게를 폐점하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Customers dropped off, so we finally decided to close the shop.

examples.ko: 그 체인점은 올해만 열 곳이 폐점했어요.
examples.en: That chain closed ten branches this year alone.
I visited one last time before it closed down.
Regular customers were sad at the news that it was closing.
I will work hard until the day we close.

explain: 가게를 아예 닫고 영업을 끝낸다는 뜻이라서, 하루 일을 마치고 문을 닫는 '문을 닫다'나 '영업을 마치다'와 달라요. 반대말은 '개점하다'이고, 완전히 닫는 경우는 '폐업하다'도 써요. 뉴스와 안내문에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means closing a shop for good and ending business, unlike '문을 닫다' or '영업을 마치다', which can mean just closing for the day. The opposite is '개점하다', and '폐업하다' is also used for a full shutdown. It often appears in news and notices.

examples.en: I sent my old car to the scrapyard.
I found a usable part at the scrapyard.
The car from the accident was moved to the scrapyard.
It's always dusty near the scrapyard.

examples.ko: 폐차장 직원이 차를 가지러 오기로 했어요.
examples.en: A scrapyard worker is coming to pick up the car.
Before going to the scrapyard, I checked the license plate first.

explain: 더 이상 못 타는 자동차를 처리하고 해체하는 곳이에요. 차를 없앨 때 '폐차하다'라고 하고, 그 일을 하는 곳이 폐차장이에요. 중고차를 파는 곳과는 달라요.
explain_en: It is the place where cars that can no longer be driven are processed and dismantled. Getting rid of a car is '폐차하다', and this is where it happens. It is different from a used-car dealership.

examples.en: I made a toy out of scrap materials.
I put out all the junk piled up at home at once.
A scrap-collecting truck is passing through the alley.
Grandfather collects scrap and sells it.
We had a recycling class using scrap at school.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 폐품을 다시 쓴 제품이에요.
examples.en: This bag is a product made from reused scrap.

explain: 못 쓰게 되어 버린 물건이지만 다시 쓰거나 팔 수 있는 것들이에요. 그냥 '쓰레기'보다는 재활용을 생각한 말이에요. '폐품 재활용', '폐품 수거'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: These are discarded things that can still be reused or sold. Unlike plain '쓰레기' (trash), the word has recycling in mind. Common phrases are '폐품 재활용' and '폐품 수거'.

examples.en: I stacked the bowls one by one and put them in the cupboard.

examples.ko: 의자를 포개 놓으면 자리를 덜 차지해요.
examples.en: If you stack the chairs, they take up less space.

examples.ko: 아이가 손을 내 손 위에 포갰어요.
examples.en: The child laid her hand on top of mine.
If you stack paper cups too high, they fall over.
If you stack the T-shirts, the closet looks neat.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 다리를 포개고 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: The two of them are sitting with their legs crossed one over the other.

explain: 같은 모양의 물건을 위에 겹쳐서 놓을 때 써요. 그릇, 의자, 손처럼 서로 맞게 겹치는 느낌이 있어요. 높이 쌓을 때는 '쌓다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 종이를 접어 겹칠 때는 '겹치다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Use it for laying items of the same shape on top of one another, like bowls, chairs or hands, so they fit together. For tall piles, '쌓다' is more common, and for overlapping paper, '겹치다' sounds natural.

examples.en: The baby fell asleep snugly in her mother's arms.
I took a nap warmly tucked under the blanket.
When snow fell, the village was softly covered.
Grandmother held me in a warm, soft hug.
The sunlight shone gently into the room.
Wrapped cozily in a blanket, the cold went away.

explain: 몸이 따뜻하고 부드럽게 감싸이는 편안한 느낌을 말해요. 이불, 품, 햇살, 분위기처럼 부드럽고 따뜻한 것과 잘 어울려요. 형용사 '포근하다'에서 온 말이라 날씨가 춥지 않고 부드러울 때도 '포근하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It conveys the comfortable feeling of being wrapped warmly and softly. It goes well with things like blankets, embraces, sunlight and atmosphere. It comes from the adjective '포근하다', which is also used for mild, soft weather.

examples.en: The baby's cheeks have filled out chubbily.

examples.ko: 강아지가 밥을 잘 먹어서 포동포동 살쪘어요.
examples.en: The puppy eats well and has gotten plump.
I met a cute child with chubby little hands.

examples.ko: 고양이 발이 포동포동해서 자꾸 만지고 싶어요.
examples.en: The cat's paws are so chubby that I keep wanting to touch them.

examples.ko: 포동포동 살이 오른 팔뚝이 정말 귀여워요.
examples.en: Those plump little arms are really adorable.

examples.ko: 병원에서 아기가 포동포동 잘 크고 있다고 했어요.
examples.en: At the clinic, they said the baby is growing nicely and plump.

explain: 아기나 작은 동물처럼 살이 보드랍게 올라 귀엽게 통통한 모습이에요. 어른에게 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있으니, 주로 아기, 강아지, 고양이에게 써요. '통통'보다 더 부드럽고 귀여운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes soft, cute plumpness, as on babies and small animals. Using it for adults can be rude, so it is mostly for babies, puppies and kittens. It feels softer and cuter than '통통'.

examples.ko: 그 선배는 포용력이 커서 모두가 좋아해요.
examples.en: That senior is so open-minded that everyone likes him.

examples.ko: 팀장에게는 실수를 받아 주는 포용력이 필요해요.
examples.en: A team leader needs the tolerance to accept mistakes.

examples.ko: 포용력 있는 사람과 일하면 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: Working with a broad-minded person puts me at ease.
I also want to develop more tolerance.

examples.ko: 그의 포용력 덕분에 갈등이 쉽게 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Thanks to his generosity, the conflict was resolved easily.
Tolerance doesn't develop overnight.

explain: 다른 사람의 단점이나 다른 생각을 넓은 마음으로 받아 주는 힘이에요. 사람의 성격을 칭찬할 때 '포용력이 있다/크다'라고 해요. '이해심'은 상대를 이해하는 마음이고, '포용력'은 그것을 품어 주는 넓이에 가까워요.
explain_en: It is the ability to accept others' faults and different views with a broad mind. You praise someone with '포용력이 있다/크다'. '이해심' is the heart to understand, while '포용력' is closer to the breadth to embrace.

examples.en: A new paved road has been built to the village.
Even when it rains, paved roads are easy to walk on.
We went through the mountain path and came out onto a paved road.
From where the paved road ends, it's a dirt road.

examples.ko: 이 길은 포장도로라서 자전거 타기 좋아요.
examples.en: This is a paved road, so it's good for cycling.
In winter the paved road froze and was slippery.

explain: 아스팔트나 시멘트로 단단하게 깔아 놓은 길이에요. 반대는 흙길이나 '비포장도로'예요. '비포장도로'는 차가 흔들려서 운전이 힘들다고 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a road laid firmly with asphalt or cement. The opposite is a dirt road, or '비포장도로'. '비포장도로' often comes up when saying the car shakes and driving is hard.
